clauses.reason: Section 1 closes all executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government and excuses their employees from duty on Tuesday, December 24, 2019 ("shall be closed and their employees excused from duty on Tuesday, December"). The text gives the reason as "the day before Christmas Day". The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on Tuesday, December 24, 2019 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past December 24, 2019. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2019-12-24, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when December 24, 2019 begins.

Section 2 lets the heads of departments and agencies decide that certain offices and installations must remain open and that certain employees must report for duty on the closed day, for reasons of national security, defense, or other public need ("December 24, 2019, for reasons of national security, defense, or other public"). It is a discretion that attaches to the closure in section 1 and has no operation once the closed day is over. The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on Tuesday, December 24, 2019 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past December 24, 2019. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2019-12-24, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when December 24, 2019 begins.

Section 3 provides that the closed day shall be considered as falling within the scope of Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b) and other similar statutes insofar as they relate to the pay and leave of employees ("December 24, 2019, shall be considered as falling within the scope"). It is a deeming rule for the closed day only. Executive Order 11582 is an earlier order cited as the pay-and-leave framework; it is not a later event and does not end this order. The pay and leave consequences for the closed day are recorded under savings. The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on Tuesday, December 24, 2019 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past December 24, 2019. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2019-12-24, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when December 24, 2019 begins.

Section 4 directs the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to take such actions as may be necessary to implement the order ("such actions as may be necessary to implement this order."). It is an implementation command with no stated date and no held record of what the Director did or when. It implements only the closure and excusal for Tuesday, December 24, 2019, so it is read as having no operation after December 24, 2019; that reading is an inference from the order's text and is disclosed, and it does not rest on any completion date. The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on Tuesday, December 24, 2019 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past December 24, 2019. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2019-12-24, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when December 24, 2019 begins.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 13900, 84 FR 69983 (Federal Register Vol. 84, No. 245, Friday, December 20, 2019; filed December 19, 2019), signed December 17, 2019 (grade official_original_counted, machine text layer of the official PDF). The heading, number, title (Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and Agencies of the Federal Government on December 24, 2019) and date agree with the census register. Text and inventory: I read the whole held text. It has sections 1 to 5 (section 5 with its sub-items), with no separate lead clause; the dossier's clause inventory matches those paragraphs and is complete. Lifecycle: the order closes the departments and agencies on Tuesday, December 24, 2019 and says nothing that runs past December 24, 2019, so every clause ends by the order's own terms on 2019-12-24 (section 5(d) excepted where it is dated separately). No later instrument names the order: the packet's lookup of held order texts for its number lists only its own Federal Register text, and the dossier's later-event chain is empty. The only other instrument the text names is Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, an earlier order cited in section 3.

Executive Order 11582 (1971) is cited in section 3 as the pay-and-leave framework; it is earlier and is not an end. A report-deadline reading does not apply because the order has no report.
